extracted.intended_audience: early-career university professors and university research administrators (potential Packard Fellowship nominees)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements for nomination, award, allowable costs, and reporting for the David and Lucile Packard Foundation Fellows program. Focused on invited institutions nominating early-career professors and on post-award administrative obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for a Packard Fellowship award
rubrics_metrics.description: Please see Eligibility and Disciplines to determine if you meet the Packard Fellowship criteria for a nomination from your university.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates should consult the Foundation's Eligibility and Disciplines page for the specific criteria that determine whether an individual is eligible to be nominated by their university.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination / application process
rubrics_metrics.description: Every January, the Foundation invites the presidents of 50 universities to nominate two early-career professors from their institutions for the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals do not apply directly; contact your university’s Office of Sponsored Research or Department Chair to learn about your institution’s internal nomination process. Only invited institutions may nominate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invited institutions limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fellowship Advisory Panel has limited the Invited Institutions list to 50 universities and nominations are only open to those universities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Invited Institutions list is periodically reviewed by the Advisory Panel to determine if institutions should be added or removed. If your institution is not on the list, you may not be nominated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award period start and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Packard Fellowship grant begins in mid-October of the year the grant is awarded. The Fellowship is a five‐year grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees should plan research timelines and budget/resource allocations around a mid-October start and a five-year funding period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect costs / allowable budget breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: The grant provides $175,000 per year for five years, subject to reasonable progress in the research work of the Fellow. Of this amount, $17,500 will be for the unrestricted use by the University and is intended to compensate for administrative costs, and the remaining $157,500 will be for the use by the Fellow to support his/her research work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget planning should reflect the fixed annual total and the designated portion for university administrative/indirect costs versus Fellow-directed research support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirements (Fellow and University)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fellow and the University are required to submit annual reports during the five-year grant. The Fellow is required to submit a one- to two-page narrative report of his/her research progress and an update of C.V. information (due October 15 via Packard Fellows Online). The University is required to submit a final financial report of the Fellow’s expenditures (due December 31 via email to Packard Fellows program staff).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows must prepare a concise annual narrative and CV update, submitted by Oct 15 through the Foundation's online portal. Universities must compile and submit the required financial reporting (final financial report of expenditures) by Dec 31 via email to program staff; ensure institutional processes are in place to meet these deadlines.
